messages.subject: Method isFinite
parts:
Hello,

I´ve checked that if we pass a Double.NA to method isFinite it returns false; however, passing an Int.NA to this method returns true.  Is this the intended behaviour?  Shouldn´t the same hold true for Double.NA and Int.NA?

Thanks,


Rodrigo

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Method isFinite
parts:
Hi Rodrigo,

Yes, this is correct, or rather, this is the only way for these two particular java methods to behave.

If you evaluate  is.na(as.double(NA_integer_)) in Renjin, it will give you what you expect (TRUE)

The behavior you're describing is that of the JVM - which doesn't know anything about NA values for integers. Both Renjin and GNU R introduce the idea of NA for integers by reserving one of the 32 bits for the NA flag. In practice, this means that at the lowest level, IntVector.NA =  -2147483648

When you call DoubleVector.isFinite(double), the JVM will implicitly cast  -2147483648 to  -2147483648.0. But of course, for 64-bit double values, we use the NaN bit + the signaling payload to represent NA. The JVM doesn't have any way of knowing that  -2147483648.0 should map to NA (Nor would want it to randomly convert -2^31 to NA either!) 

This is logic that we have to implement ourselves. So you can use IntVector.isNA(x) instead of DoubleVector.isNA() as NA is the only non-finite value in the R integer domain.

HTH,

Alex
